ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as crude oil prices slid below $90 a barrel—U.S. crude dropped to $89.53—and broader headwinds hit energy stocks. The collapse of climate talks at COP31, which failed to include fossil fuels in the final agreement, signals that oil demand faces fewer regulatory constraints than some had feared, but it also underscores growing investor concern about the sector's long-term prospects. Meanwhile, analysts are signaling that the refinery boom that drove energy stocks higher is cooling off, pushing money away from the sector.

The stock has now fallen roughly $8 (or 5.6%) from its peak two weeks ago as oil prices retreated and sentiment shifted. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—recent Houthi and Iranian attacks on Saudi refineries—have done little to support prices, suggesting that even supply-side concerns are being overwhelmed by demand weakness or expectations that markets remain adequately supplied.
